items.title: Gap Mangione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: First of all, it came about with Stan Kenton and his jazz summer camps, where he would take the band... bring them into a college and hook up a performance, a person-to-person connection with the guys in the band and the students

ctx.x: Do you have any opinions or a take on jazz education?

Oh I think it’s fantastic. For fifteen years I gave one course a year at Syracuse University, the History of Jazz. A lot of people thought I was teaching piano. The History of Jazz. And during this time I’ve brought up — the subject of jazz education comes up. And first of all I don’t think that anybody can teach jazz as such. You can’t find somebody who’s just not a jazz player and make him a jazz player. Now you can give this person the tools, the comprehension of music generally, the capability to play an…
